body: Case-sensitivity bug: the SQL lowercases the stored `host` column but compares it to `uri.host` without lowercasing it. `URI('http://EvilTrout.com').host` returns 'EvilTrout.com', so a referer with any uppercase letters is rejected. Use `host.downcase` (or `lower(?)`).

The validation regex allows a port (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`), so admins can save `example.com:8080`. But `record_for_host` compares against `uri.host`, which never includes the port, so such a host will never match. Either strip or reject ports on save, or compare against host+port. Also, TLDs longer than 5 chars (e.g. `.museum`, `.technology`) and single-label hosts like `localhost` are rejected, even though the old site-setting accepted them.

`self.host.sub!` raises NoMethodError when `host` is nil, e.g. `EmbeddableHost.new.valid?` or a create/update request with no `host` param. That produces a 500 instead of a validation error. Guard it with `if host.present?`. Also, `sub!` mutates the caller's string in place.

This crashes when `embed_category` was never set, which is the common case because site_settings rows only exist for non-default values. `execute(...)[0]` is then nil and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError, so the migration fails on most installs. The same problem hits line 16 when `uncategorized_category_id` isn't stored in site_settings. Handle empty results; for example, fall back to the uncategorized category looked up from the categories table.

Host values are interpolated into the SQL without quoting or escaping, so a value containing `'` breaks the migration. Values are also not stripped or normalized: `\r` from `\r\n` line endings, blank lines, and `http://` prefixes and paths are inserted as-is. The old code accepted `http://discourse.org` and matched its URI host; after migration the row won't match `lower(host) = uri.host`, so existing embeds silently stop working. Normalize the values (strip the scheme and path, downcase, skip blanks) and use a quoted or parameterized insert.

The migration deletes the old site settings irreversibly inside `change`, so rolling back loses the embeddable host config. Consider splitting it into `up`/`down`. Also, `create_table ... force: true` would silently drop an existing table.

`EmbeddableHost.where(id: ...).first` returns nil for an unknown id, so `host.destroy` (and `save_host(host)` in `update`) raises NoMethodError and returns a 500. Use `find` (404) or check for nil explicitly.

`params[:embeddable_host][:host]` raises NoMethodError when the `embeddable_host` key is missing; use `params.require(:embeddable_host)`. `category_id` is also not checked against existing categories, so any integer is accepted and later breaks `category-badge` and topic creation. Also, `ensure_logged_in, :ensure_staff` is redundant or weaker: Admin::AdminController already requires admin.

When the URL's host has no EmbeddableHost record (for example, feed-polled items from a host that isn't whitelisted), `eh` is nil and the category silently becomes nil. Previously the `embed_category` setting applied to all embeds. That's a behavior change: feed-imported topics that used to go to the configured category now end up uncategorized.
`type.replace('_', '-')` only replaces the first underscore. Any model type with two or more underscores won't be normalized. Use `/_/g`.

The new `_ids` branch assumes `obj[k]` is an array. Any payload key ending in `_ids` that is null, or not an id list for a hydratable type, will throw on `.map`, or replace the key with an array of undefined. This changes behavior for every REST model with `*_ids` attributes, which previously were left untouched. `hydrated || []` is also a no-op because `map` always returns an array. Unresolved lookups should be filtered out, and the key should only be deleted when hydration succeeds, matching the singular branch.
`destroyRecord()` has no `.catch(popupAjaxError)`, unlike `save`, so failures are silently swallowed and the row stays in place with no feedback.

If no category is chosen, the server defaults to the uncategorized category, but the client sets `host.category` to `Discourse.Category.findById(null)` (undefined). The row then shows no badge until reload. Use the `category_id` returned by the server response instead.

The file contents appear swapped: `category_fabricator.rb` now defines the `:embeddable_host` fabricator, and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains all the category fabricators. It works only because every fabricator file gets loaded, but it's confusing and breaks the naming convention. Swap them back.
